channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Fed Chair Warsh to note they have no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation
item.description: According to the prepared remarks that Federal Reserve (Fed) Chairman Kevin Warsh will deliver during his testimony on the Semiannual Monetary Policy Report before the US House Financial Services Committee, he will note that the Fed has no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah : Under pressure with hawkish BI bias – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale notes Bank Indonesia’s (BI) reaction function is driven by the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) and exchange rate stability. The report says the Rupiah faces pressure from a stronger US Dollar (USD) and hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) pricing, with stress around USD/IDR 18,000.

item.title: Hungary: Growth outlook getting brighter – ING
item.description: ING economists Peter Virovacz and Frantisek Taborsky turn more optimistic on Hungary’s growth outlook, noting positive surprises in high-frequency data and stronger consumption. They still project 1.5% GDP growth in 2026 but now see clear upside risks.

item.title: Euro jumps as softer-than-expected US CPI cools bets on rate hikes
item.description: EUR/USD snaps a two-day losing streak on Tuesday as softer-than-expected United States (US) inflation data weighs on the US Dollar (USD) and prompts traders to scale back expectations of a near-term Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike.

item.title: European Union: Growth potential re-rated – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Julie Ioffe and James Rossiter argue that the European Union already possesses key ingredients for stronger long-term growth, including wealthy consumers, productive workers, deep private savings and solid fiscal capacity.

item.title: Gold rises 2% as soft US CPI cools Fed rate-hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rebounds sharply on Tuesday, erasing losses recorded on the previous day after softer-than-expected US inflation data eased expectations of a near-term Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike.

item.title: Natural Gas: Higher winter gas risk priced in – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank revises its TTF Natural Gas and JKM forecasts higher for Q3 and Q4 2026, citing a structurally tight LNG market and deeper Qatari export losses following renewed Hormuz disruption.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ hawkish repricing supports Kiwi – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman reports the New Zealand Dollar is the top G10 performer overnight, helped by a hawkish shift in RBNZ rate expectations.

item.title: Breaking: US CPI inflation softens to 3.5% in June vs. 3.8% expected
item.description: Annual inflation in the United States (US), as measured by the change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), declined to 3.5% in June from the three-year high it set at 4.2% in May, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported on Tuesday. This print came in well below the market expectation of 3.8%.

item.title: Euro: Rate support at risk against US Dollar with energy shock – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole argues that the EUR/USD short-term rate differential is currently supporting the Euro as Gulf tensions rise, helped by a recovery in EUR front-end rates.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Buyers defend 216.50 as bullish trend continues
item.description: GBP/JPY trades in a narrow range on Tuesday as market sentiment remains fragile amid escalating tensions between the US and Iran, which are driving Oil prices higher once again. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 217.10 as the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains broadly weak.

item.title: Japanese Yen: JGB outperformance and repatriation story – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes USD/JPY is trading near a 40‑year high above 162.00 while Japanese Government Bonds are outperforming. Strong demand at the 20‑year auction and comments from Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama encouraging more domestic investment support JGBs.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar hits fresh three-month highs as central banks divergence hurts the Aussie
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) extended gains against the Aussie Dollar (AUD) on Tuesday.

item.title: US Dollar: Inflation risks skewed to downside – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister argues recent US Dollar strength rests on increasingly hawkish Federal Reserve expectations that may be overdone.

item.title: United States Dollar Index holds correction near 101.10, eyes on inflation data
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) holds its early corrective move in Tuesday’s European session ahead of the United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) data for June, which will be published at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: Brent: Refined products risk contrasts resilient crude – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists Joe DeLaura and Florence Schmit keep their Brent Oil forecasts broadly unchanged, projecting $80/bbl in Q3 2026 and $78/bbl in Q4 2026.

item.title: US Dollar: Residual strength as safe-haven returns – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect the US Dollar to retain some residual strength in Q3 as positioning normalizes and traditional safe-haven demand returns.

item.title: Copper: Physical demand supports prices – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey highlight supportive fundamentals for Copper, with tightening LME warehouse dynamics and strong physical demand.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: 20-day EMA continues to be key barrier
item.description: The AUD/USD pair trades 0.35% higher to near 0.6945 during the European trading session on Tuesday. The Aussie pair gains as the US Dollar (USD) underperforms its peers ahead of the United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) data for June, which will be published at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed pricing stays hawkish – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that the rebound in Oil is lifting US inflation expectations and supporting the Dollar. Haddad highlights sticky US inflation, a resilient labor market and US economic outperformance as factors keeping Fed pricing hawkish.

item.title: Fed: Data-driven path through summer – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Christoph Rieger argues that US CPI and Fed Chair Warsh’s testimony will shape Fed expectations over summer, with markets currently pricing roughly a 50/50 chance of a July hike and more than 25bp by September.

item.title: WTI Oil holds at monthly highs around $80.00 as Iran’s conflict escalates
item.description: Oil prices extend gains on Tuesday, with the barrel of the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) consolidating at one-month highs in the $80.00 area, trading about 18% above the lows seen in early July.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD rebounds above $4,000 with US CPI in focus
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) is up 0.5% to near $4,020 during the European trading session on Tuesday. The precious metal gains as the US Dollar (USD) corrects ahead of the United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) data for June, which will be published at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: Indian Rupee slumps as oil prices surge, US CPI data awaited
item.description: The Indian Rupee trades significantly lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday. The USD/INR pair posts a fresh seven-week high near 96.20 as surging oil prices and United States (US) Treasury Yields due to threats of levy from Washington have weakened the appeal of the Indian currency.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Domestic savings shift aids JGBs and JPY – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes Japanese government bond yields have fallen despite higher global yields, with Japanese Government Bonds (JGBs) supported by verbal intervention from policymakers.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Pound holds above 1.3350 with the 200-day SMA capping gains
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) appreciates against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday to trim previous losses and return to the 1.3375 area, aiming to retest resistance at the key 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA).

item.title: US Dollar: Tailwinds build as oil and Fed reprice – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note the US Dollar (USD) has strengthened broadly on higher Oil prices, hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) rhetoric and softer risk sentiment.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Gulf re-escalation favours Kiwi outperformance – ING
item.description: ING strategist Francesco Pesole notes that the New Zealand Dollar is the best-performing G10 currency since early week, boosted by last week’s RBNZ rate hike and hawkish repricing. He says FX markets are rewarding currencies with scope for further domestic tightening, beyond commodity exposure.

item.title: Fed: Guidance, reaction function and rates – BNY
item.description: BNY Markets strategists John Velis and David Tam discuss new Federal Reserve (Fed) task forces and focus on the Communications group led by Mervyn King, Arminio Fraga and Peter Fisher.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Tuesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $58.08 per troy ounce, up 0.76% from the $57.65 it cost on Monday.
